results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** A smooth manifold $X$ with an auxiliary Riemannian metric; a compact interval $J$; an embedded smooth curve $\beta$ with $\dot\beta\ne0$; and compatible smooth formal scalar jets $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$ on a finite coordinate cover of a tube around $\beta(J)$.

[F1] [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]: the auxiliary metric is smooth and positive definite; [[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-riemannian-geometry]] supplies its Levi–Civita connection.

[F3] [[lem-ip-smooth-whitney-extension-on-compact-sets]]: continuous all-order ambient jets on a compact Euclidean set with full Whitney remainder compatibility have a choice-free smooth realization, uniformly when the bounds and moduli are common.

[F2] [[thm-local-existence-uniqueness-and-smooth-dependence-for-manifold-integral-curves]]: the geodesic ODE has local solutions with smooth dependence on initial data, so the normal exponential map is smooth and has the identity differential on each zero-section fiber.



1.1 First handle the endpoints, rather than taking an inverse chart on a closed parameter interval. In a coordinate chart at $\beta(a)$, extend the coordinate curve through $a$ as follows. For $t<0$ use the Borel series $\sum_{j\ge0}v_jt^j\chi(t/r_j)/j!$, where $v_j=\partial_s^j\beta(a)$ and a fixed smooth $\chi$ equals one near zero and has compact support. Choose $r_j$ to be the largest dyadic number at most $2^{-j}$ for which every derivative of order $m<j$ of the $j$th summand is bounded by $2^{-j}$; such a radius exists since these bounds are constants times $r_j^{j-m}$. The tails converge with all fixed derivatives, and their derivatives at zero are the prescribed $v_j$. Join this negative-side series to the original curve for $t\ge0$; matching all one-sided derivatives makes the join smooth. Repeat at $b$. The nonzero endpoint derivatives persist after shrinking the two extensions. They remain embedded: within each endpoint chart a coordinate with nonzero tangent derivative is strictly monotone; the endpoint image is separated from the compact remainder of the original curve, and the two distinct endpoint neighborhoods can be made disjoint. Thus $\beta$ extends to an embedded open interval containing $J$. Apply the identical endpoint series separately to each transverse jet coefficient and each endpoint; use its one-sided derivatives for $v_j$. For a bounded compact parameter family, take the uniform coefficient-derivative bounds in the finite inequalities defining $r_j$, so the radii and all extension seminorm bounds are common. This is a deterministic construction for the countable coefficient family, not an appeal to a choice of extensions. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 For the extended curve the normal exponential map $E(s,y)=\exp_{\beta(s)}y$ maps its normal bundle into $X$. Its derivative at $(s,0)$ sends the parameter direction to $\dot\beta(s)$ and is the identity on the normal directions, hence is an isomorphism by [F1] and [F2]. The inverse function theorem gives open local tube charts, including at the original endpoints. A uniform tube over a slightly larger compact interval exists: if injectivity failed at every shrinking radius, compactness would give two collisions converging to zero-section points, which embeddedness identifies; one local inverse chart then excludes them. Thus the tube image contains an open neighborhood of all of $\beta(J)$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given, construct]

3.1 In one tube chart write the extended prescribed transverse Taylor series as $\sum_{k\ge0}P_k(s,y)$, with $P_k$ homogeneous of degree $k$ in $y$. Fix a smooth transverse cutoff equal to one near zero. For each $m<k$, let $C_{k,m}$ bound the derivatives of total order at most $m$ of $P_k(s,y)\chi(|y|/\epsilon)$ after removing the factor $\epsilon^{k-m}$, on the slightly extended compact parameter interval. Define explicitly $$\epsilon_k=\min\left\{2^{-k},\min_{0\le m<k}\left(\frac{2^{-k}}{1+C_{k,m}}\right)^{1/(k-m)}\right\}.$$ Every derivative of order $m<k$ of the $k$th cutoff summand is then bounded by $2^{-k}$. Therefore $F_i=\sum_k P_k\chi(|y|/\epsilon_k)$ is smooth on the open tube and has exactly the prescribed transverse jet: a cutoff is constant near zero, so the homogeneous polynomial contributes its own degree and no other. Step 1.1 and uniform coefficient bounds make these choices common for the stated parameter families. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Choose a finite smooth partition supported in the tube charts and summing to one near $\beta(J)$. The local realizations have the same full jets along the curve, since transverse data and their tangential derivatives determine them and the given coordinate chain rule identifies them. The Leibniz formula therefore makes the partition-weighted sum realize the same jets. In particular, derivatives of the partition sum of positive order vanish, and its zeroth derivative is one. This proves the original single-segment claim on an open neighborhood, including its endpoints, with no choice axiom. [step 2.1, step 3.1, given, construct, algebra]

5.1 For the finite union, first take the induced full ambient jets specified in the Statement. Cover its compact image by finitely many smaller coordinate patches with closures inside larger patches. The intersection of the union with each smaller closed patch is compact; by the full Whitney hypothesis its coordinate jets meet [F3] in every order. Apply [F3] componentwise (two real components for complex values) and restrict the resulting smooth realization to the smaller patch. A finite smooth partition of unity on a neighborhood of the union now combines these realizations: at each point of the union all active realizations have its same full jet, so the same Leibniz cancellation as in step 4.1 applies. Uniform coefficient bounds and uniform Whitney moduli give common extension scales in [F3], hence uniform seminorms after this fixed finite partition. Pointwise compatibility only at intersections would not suffice for this step; the stated Whitney remainder condition controls pairs of nearby points on different segments as well. This proves the entire finite-union assertion and its parameter-uniform form. [F3, step 4.1, given, construct, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The compact set and all-order Whitney field in the statement, or a family on that fixed set with uniform coefficient bounds and remainder moduli.

[F1] [[thm-whitney-extension-for-finite-order-euclidean-jets]] gives a choice-free $C^k$ extension of each finite compatible jet by its explicit dyadic Whitney-cube partition and lexicographically selected nearest points.



1.1 The empty-set case has the zero extension. Otherwise use the fixed Whitney cubes and partition $\psi_Q$ constructed in [F1]: outside $A$, their side lengths satisfy $\ell(Q)\asymp\operatorname{dist}(Q,A)$, enlarged cubes have bounded overlap and comparable sizes when they meet, and $|D^\alpha\psi_Q|\le C_\alpha\ell(Q)^{-|\alpha|}$. These facts follow from the fixed maximal dyadic retention test and rescaled bump quotient in that proof, independently of the jet order. Put $\sigma(z)=\sum_Q\ell(Q)\psi_Q(z)$. This is smooth and positive off $A$, and for $t=\operatorname{dist}(z,A)$ it satisfies $c t\le\sigma(z)\le C t$ and $|D^\alpha\sigma(z)|\le C_\alpha t^{1-|\alpha|}$. Each derivative estimate follows by bounded overlap and the side-length comparison. Fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $\chi=1$ on $(-\infty,1]$ and $\chi=0$ on $[2,\infty)$. Then $\eta_\delta(z)=\chi(\sigma(z)/\delta)$ equals one for $t\le\delta/C$, vanishes for $t\ge2\delta/c$, and obeys $|D^\alpha\eta_\delta|\le B_\alpha t^{-|\alpha|}$ on its transition, with constants independent of $\delta$. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 For each integer $k\ge1$, take the actual extension $H_k$ produced by [F1]'s fixed cube formula for $P_a^k$. It is $C^k$ everywhere and smooth off $A$, since there it is a locally finite sum of smooth partition functions times polynomials. All these extensions are thereby specified without selecting elements of unspecified nonempty sets. Put $\Delta_k=H_{k+1}-H_k$. It is $C^k$ and all its derivatives through order $k$ vanish on $A$. Taylor's formula at a nearest point of $A$, on a fixed compact neighborhood of $A$, gives for every $|\beta|\le k$ $$|D^\beta\Delta_k(z)|=o(t^{k-|\beta|})\qquad(t=\operatorname{dist}(z,A)\downarrow0),$$ uniformly near $A$. Indeed the top derivative is uniformly continuous and zero on $A$, and the lower estimates follow by Taylor's integral remainder along the segment from the nearest point. In the parameter-family case these remainders are uniform: the finite-order cube proof bounds $D^\alpha H_k-D^\alpha P_{a_z}^k$ by a constant times the specified Whitney remainder modulus; away from $A$ on a compact set its locally finite formula bounds every derivative by the coefficient bounds. Hence the $C^k$ moduli at $A$ used here are common to the family. [F1, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 The product rule and step 1.1 show that, for $|\alpha|\le k$, $D^\alpha(\eta_\delta\Delta_k)$ is bounded by a constant $B_k$ times $\max_{|\beta|\le k}t^{|\beta|-|\alpha|}|D^\beta\Delta_k|$, wherever $\eta_\delta$ is nonzero. Choose $\delta_k$ as the largest dyadic number $2^{-j}$ satisfying $\delta_k\le2^{-k}$, $\delta_k\le\delta_{k-1}/2$ when $k>1$, and the finitely many uniform inequalities $$B_k|D^\beta\Delta_k(z)|\le2^{-k}t^{k-|\beta|}\quad(0<t\le2\delta_k/c,\ |\beta|\le k).$$ The set of admissible integers $j$ is nonempty by step 2.1 and has a least element, so these scales are deterministic. Enlarge $B_k$ to include the finitely many binomial constants. Then $$|D^\alpha(\eta_{\delta_k}\Delta_k)(z)|\le2^{-k}t^{k-|\alpha|}\qquad(|\alpha|\le k).$$ Uniform moduli in step 2.1 give the same scales for the parameter family. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Define off $A$ $$F=H_1+\sum_{k\ge1}\eta_{\delta_k}(H_{k+1}-H_k),$$ and set $F(a)=f_0(a)$ on $A$. At each point off $A$ the sum is locally finite because $\delta_k\to0$, so $F$ is smooth there. Fix $K\ge1$. Sufficiently near $A$, all factors $\eta_{\delta_k}$ with $k<K$ equal one, and telescoping gives $F-H_K=\sum_{k\ge K}\eta_{\delta_k}\Delta_k$. For $|\alpha|\le K$, the single $k=K$ term is $o(t^{K-|\alpha|})$ by step 2.1 and the product rule, while the sum over $k>K$ is $O(t^{K+1-|\alpha|})$ by step 3.1 and a geometric series, taking $t<1/2$. Thus every derivative through order $K$ of this difference off $A$ is $o(t^{K-|\alpha|})$. Extend the difference by zero on $A$. These estimates make its order-$K$ derivatives continuous and zero there; for lower orders the first-order difference quotient at any $a\in A$ tends to zero since $t\le|z-a|$, so induction verifies that the continuous derivative extensions are actual derivatives. Therefore $F-H_K$ is $C^K$ with zero $K$-jet on $A$. Since $H_K$ has the prescribed $K$-jet and $K$ is arbitrary, $F$ is smooth and realizes the entire field. The same estimates are uniform for the parameter family near $A$, and local finiteness gives uniform bounds on every compact set away from $A$. This proves the uniform assertion and completes the choice-free construction. [step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎
